title: POC Weekly: Latency Tuning - RiverMark
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on reducing TTFT and overall tail latency. Reviewed last week's benchmark where TTFT with streaming off was ~360ms p50 and enabling streaming + kernel fallback reduced p50 to ~230ms but increased tail. Agreed to run two targeted benchmarks: 1) 512 seq streaming with small-kernel path and kv cache warm, 2) 256 seq cold-start simulation on dedicated nodes. Next steps: Redwood to share kernel config and perf runbooks; RiverMark to provide exact traffic profile and env access for dedicated runs.
next_steps: Redwood: Share kernel config & perf runbook (by 2027-02-25)
RiverMark: Provide sample traffic CSV + peak percentiles (by 2027-02-25)
Joint: Run two benchmark permutations on dedicated nodes (schedule week of 2027-03-01)
Redwood: Send updated POC run results and cost delta estimate (after benchmarks)
action_items: Alex Kim: Upload kernel config and step-by-step perf runbook; due 2027-02-25
Liam O'Connor: Share production traffic profile CSV and p95/p99 targets; due 2027-02-25
Jordan Lee: Schedule dedicated-node benchmark and provide command lines; due 2027-03-01
Sofia Martinez: Confirm access level for Redwood test user in dev VPC; due 2027-02-24
questions: Can we reproduce TTFT improvements on dedicated vs hosted?
How much does enabling streaming increase p99 tail?
Which kernel fallback gave best average latency in last run?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-23 14:00 ET, Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM) \u0014 RiverMark: Sofia Martinez, Liam O'Connor, Evelyn Reed, Noah Vega

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick agenda \u0014 review last week's perf runs, TTFT numbers, streaming effects, and agree next benchmarks.
[00:15] Sofia Martinez: yeah thanks Alex. we saw the spreadsheet, quick context \u0014 our SLAs are p95 < 500ms and p99 < 900ms for the inference path, TTFT ideally sub-300ms.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: got it. recap from Redwood side \u0014 last run on hosted with model v1-rc we measured cold TTFT p50 ~360ms, p95 ~780ms. when we enabled streaming + kernel "small-attn" fallback we dropped p50 to ~230ms but p99 moved up slightly to ~920ms.
[00:50] Noah Vega: sorry can you clarify small-attn? is that a custom kernel or quantized path? transcript note: sometimes the auto transcript says small at n \u0014
[01:05] Jordan Lee: yeah, small-attn is our lighter kernel path for shorter sequences, it's not quantized per se but uses optimized attention kernels and reduced kernel launch overhead; when the sequence is short we route to that.
[01:25] Liam O'Connor: and streaming was off originally?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: original baseline had streaming off \u0014 full response emitted at once. enabling streaming reduces time-to-first-token because we start sending tokens before the full generation completes. that improves TTFT but can increase p99 if batching changes or if we hit tail scheduling.
[01:50] Evelyn Reed: we worry about tail spikes, our users are sensitive so p99 is as important as p50.
[01:55] Alex Kim: totally, so tradeoff conversation. we looked at two levers last week: streaming + kernel routing and kv cache warm vs cold. when KV cache is warm (i.e., repeated prefixes) we saw p50 ~180ms on streaming + small-attn, p95 ~420ms. cold-start scenarios pushed those up.
[02:20] Sofia Martinez: what was the sequence length distribution you used? our average request is ~120 tokens but we have spikes to 512 occasionally.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: we used synthetic mix: 70% short (<=128), 25% mid (129-256), 5% long (257-512). we should test a 100% 512 run to simulate the spike scenario you mentioned.
[02:45] Liam O'Connor: from infra perspective we also want to know kernel memory usage \u0014 sometimes the small kernel has higher setup overhead on particular GPU drivers. did you see any OOMs?
[02:55] Jordan Lee: no OOMs in our runs, but we did see higher CPU-side kernel-launch latency for some combinations, especially with host-side batching enabled. some of that is driver variance.
[03:10] Alex Kim: quick note \u0014 the automated routing sometimes mislabels the kernel as kv cash in the transcript (ha), so ignore that.
[03:20] (laughter)
[03:25] Noah Vega: ok practical question: for TTFT do you measure from request arrival at LB to first token out?
[03:30] Jordan Lee: yes measured at the Redwood ingress-to-egress path. for your internal metrics you might measure differently at the proxy, so we agreed to align measurement points in the bench.
[03:45] Sofia Martinez: good. want to go through the run we did Tuesday?
[03:50] Jordan Lee: sure. Tuesday's runs summary: baseline hosted non-streaming p50 360ms / p95 780ms / p99 1.02s. streaming + small-attn on same hosted fleet: p50 230ms / p95 820ms / p99 1.1s. dedicated nodes with streaming and kernel tuning: p50 200ms / p95 480ms / p99 640ms. so dedicated looks promising for tail.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: that's helpful \u2014 what config did you use for the dedicated nodes? GPU type, batch size, quantization?
[04:30] Jordan Lee: dedicated was 2x A100-80GB with int8 quantization on FFN kernels, dynamic batching with max tokens-per-batch set to 2048, sequence-length aware routing enabled. also we pinned model to a single node pool to avoid cross-pool scheduling.
[04:50] Evelyn Reed: int8 on FFN \u2014 any quality impact on outputs?
[04:55] Jordan Lee: minimal for your evaluation prompts, we ran a small eval set and saw negligible metric drift, but we'll include the exact eval results in the runbook.
[05:10] Alex Kim: about kernel choices \u2014 question for Sean (not on call) \u2014 we used the small-attn kernel for <=128 sequences, medium-attn for 129-256, and fallback to generic for >256. there was a bug observed where fallback sometimes forced a cold kernel launch increasing latency; we've fixed that in the staging build.
[05:35] Sofia Martinez: great. so immediate experiments to run?
[05:40] Jordan Lee: propose two benchmark permutations: A) 512-seq streaming enabled on dedicated nodes with kv cache pre-warmed (simulate sustained load so cache stays warm). B) 256-seq mix but simulate cold-starts at 10% traffic (cache miss) and measure TTFT+p99.
[06:00] Noah Vega: how will we simulate cold starts? restart containers between subtests?
[06:05] Jordan Lee: we'll flush the KV cache and spin up new worker processes between runs to approximate cold conditions; we can also vary startup concurrency.
[06:15] Liam O'Connor: can Redwood run the dedicated benchmarks in our dev VPC or do we provide logs and you run in your dedicated fleet?
[06:22] Alex Kim: either works. easier for reproducibility if we run in your dev VPC dedicated nodes \u2014 we need a test user with limited IAM and network access. Sofia, can you confirm?
[06:34] Sofia Martinez: yes we'll create a test role. action item for me.
[06:38] (10 sec silence)
[06:48] Jordan Lee: one more note on streaming \u2014 to reduce p99 we sometimes limit per-request concurrency so streaming doesn't block larger batches; it's an adaptive knob. also adjusting max tokens-per-batch influences tail heavily.
[07:05] Evelyn Reed: curious about cost delta \u2014 dedicated looks better for tail but cost per token higher?
[07:12] Alex Kim: on our figures, dedicated with kernel tuning reduced total cost per token by ~12% vs hosted for your observed load, mainly due to better packing and reduced overprovision. but committed reserved instances are required to get those numbers. we'll provide a cost sheet.
[07:30] Noah Vega: can you put numbers for the two benchmark permutations? estimate run time and expected improvement?
[07:36] Jordan Lee: yes. permutation A expected to show TTFT p50 ~190-220ms and p99 under 700ms if cache stays warm. permutation B expected to show p99 closer to 900-1.1s for cold-start spikes. we'll include confidence intervals.
[07:55] Sofia Martinez: also include driver/OS matrix \u2014 we run both RHEL8 and Ubuntu 22.04, driver versions differ. we need notes if a particular driver causes higher kernel-launch times.
[08:06] Jordan Lee: good call. we'll document GPU driver matrix and any recommended versions.
[08:10] Alex Kim: ok quick check \u2014 are we aligned on metrics? we'll report TTFT (ingress->first-token), total latency (request->final-token), p50/p95/p99, and tail jitter.
[08:22] Liam O'Connor: yes and add CPU utilization and kernel launch counts.
[08:26] Jordan Lee: Roger.
[08:30] Maya Patel: I'll bundle those into the runbook and share.
[08:34] (brief cross talk)
[08:40] Sofia Martinez: any blockers on our side?
[08:42] Liam O'Connor: just the test role and sample traffic CSV, we can get that today.
[08:47] Sofia Martinez: ok I'll do it.
[08:50] Alex Kim: perfect. let's open the floor for technical deep dive questions \u2014 Evan? (Evelyn?)
[09:00] Evelyn Reed: yes one question \u2014 how do you handle batching for streaming requests? are they batched differently?
[09:07] Jordan Lee: streaming requests are batched but we prioritize first-token generation; batching window is adaptive \u2014 we use a short window (e.g., 10ms) for first-token aggregation then longer windows for continuation tokens. that reduces TTFT while keeping throughput. it's tunable.
[09:30] Noah Vega: any problems with GRPC vs REST for TTFT?
[09:35] Jordan Lee: gRPC typically gives slightly lower serialization overhead; on our numbers it's ~10-15ms improvement for TTFT vs REST in similar infra. but your proxy stack might negate that.
[09:50] Sofia Martinez: we'll try gRPC in the next bench.
[09:53] Alex Kim: noted.
[09:56] (pause)
[10:10] Jordan Lee: practical note \u2014 kernel selection is sensitive to seq-length misclassification. if your tokenizer outputs sometimes mis-estimate token counts, requests can be routed to suboptimal kernels \u2014 recommend validating tokenization pipeline.
[10:28] Liam O'Connor: we'll run token count distribution from prod logs and send it.
[10:32] Sofia Martinez: question about fallbacks \u2014 what happens if small-attn fails at runtime?
[10:36] Jordan Lee: we fall back to generic kernel; there's a small latency penalty during the fallback window. we now have a prewarm path that avoids cold-launch if the fallback is predicted. we've enabled that on the staging build we used.
[10:55] Alex Kim: ok time check, 30 minutes in. quick round for confirmations and owners.
[11:00] Sofia Martinez: RiverMark will provide traffic CSV and create test role by tomorrow (2027-02-24).
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: assigned.
[11:08] Alex Kim: Redwood will share kernel config and perf runbook by 2027-02-25 and schedule dedicated benchmark week of 2027-03-01.
[11:15] Maya Patel: I'll send calendar invites and the runbook link.
[11:20] Noah Vega: one last question \u2014 do you have a recommended streaming chunk size?
[11:24] Jordan Lee: default 16 tokens is typical, but for low-latency TTFT we sometimes go to 8 tokens; smaller chunks increase overhead but reduce first-byte latency. tune per workload.
[11:40] Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone. last ask \u2014 include an explicit test that measures cold-start at 0% cache and then 30s steady state.
[11:48] Jordan Lee: will do.
[11:50] Alex Kim: awesome, we'll follow up with the artifact links and benchmark schedule. thanks all.
[12:00] Call ended.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash). Links shared: runbook: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/rm-latency-2027-02, perf sheet: https://redwood.example.com/perf/rm-poc-2027-02-sheet
